title: Congenital heart defects
claims: Systemic return: RA → RV → pulmonary artery. Pulmonary return: LA → LV → aorta.
Left-sided pressures exceed right-sided, so a hole between the sides shunts left → right unless the right side is obstructed.
ASD: left-to-right shunt at atrial level (ostium secundum most common; ostium primum is associated with Down syndrome).
ASD: right atrial/ventricular volume overload and increased pulmonary flow.
ASD: fixed split S2; systolic ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border (extra flow across the pulmonic valve).
ASD: paradoxical embolism is possible. Eisenmenger if the shunt reverses.
VSD: most common congenital heart defect; membranous septum is the usual site.
VSD: left-to-right shunt; holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border (smaller defects are louder).
VSD: large defects cause pulmonary overcirculation, heart failure, then pulmonary hypertension and Eisenmenger (shunt reverses, cyanosis, clubbing).
PDA: persistent channel between the descending aorta (just distal to the left subclavian) and the left pulmonary artery.
PDA: left-to-right shunt: continuous “machinery” murmur, bounding pulses, wide pulse pressure.
PDA: associated with prematurity and maternal rubella. Closure: indomethacin/ibuprofen. If a ductus-dependent lesion exists, keep it open with prostaglandin E1.
Tetralogy of Fallot: four features: pulmonary (infundibular) stenosis, RVH, overriding aorta, VSD.
Tetralogy of Fallot: right-to-left shunt across the VSD → cyanosis. “Tet spells” improve with squatting (raises SVR, pushes blood toward the lungs).
Tetralogy of Fallot: boot-shaped heart on CXR. Associated with 22q11 deletion. Classically the most common cyanotic CHD beyond infancy.
TGA: aorta arises from the RV; pulmonary artery from the LV → two parallel circuits.
TGA: not compatible with life without mixing (PDA, ASD or VSD). Cyanosis in the first days of life.
TGA: “egg on a string” CXR (narrow mediastinum). Associated with maternal diabetes.
TGA: keep the ductus open with prostaglandin E1; definitive fix is the arterial switch.
